description: Vectors of the schemas of structure version 1 (docs/api-stability.md, section 9), chapter 1: what is signed and what travels. Built by tests/schema_vectors.py with tests/schema_reference.py; tests/vectors/kern/profile_check.go checks them with tables of its own (-schemas). `accepted` holds objects that are of their schema on the network `network_id`. `refused` holds objects that are not: an accepted object (`from`) with members removed (`remove`), then values put in place (`set`), or an object of its own; `rule` names the rule that refuses it, by a key of `rules`. A path is names of members and positions in lists joined by full stops, and a value put one position past the end of a list is added to it. Objects are written with the `directives`. `bytes` is the length of the canonical encoding of the object once its directives are carried out, and `pin` the first 8 bytes of the SHA3-384 of that encoding: they only show that two programs built the same object. The fillers are not keys, and no signature here verifies: a schema does not verify signatures. `mutations`, where present, asks for more: every object one change away from this one is refused, except this one without a member listed in `optional`. The changes: every array and every object replaced by the string x, and nothing more in the ones listed in `free`; elsewhere, every member of an object removed in turn, and a member zz of value 0 added, except in the objects listed in `maps`; every string replaced by 0, every boolean by 1, every integer by its digits as a string, then by true. `accepted_texts` and `refused_texts` are texts as a node receives them: the size of a frame and the nesting are checked on the bytes, then the canonical encoding, then the schema; the schema `json` is any value of canonical JSON, and `prefix` is the four bytes that precede the text in a frame. An accepted object of the schema `frame` has its `prefix` too: the length of its canonical encoding, most significant byte first, and nothing else. `prefixes` holds four bytes as a node reads them before a frame: `announces` is the number of bytes that follow, and `rule` refuses those that announce more than `frame_bytes`, which bounds what follows and does not count the four bytes. `answers` holds what a node sends in answer to a `get_blocks` from `from` to `to`: `held` lists the blocks it holds, each as a level and the bytes of its final block in the frame, and `levels` the levels of the blocks of its answer; a frame without a block is 29 bytes, and each block after the first adds a comma. `replies` holds answers as the node that asked sees them, by the levels of their blocks: accepted, or refused by `rule`.

rules.not_canonical: the bytes are not the canonical JSON of a value
rules.too_deep: arrays and objects are nested beyond the bound
rules.too_long: the encoding of a frame, a transaction, the transactions of a block or a claim is beyond its bound
rules.wrong_type: the value is not of the JSON type its schema gives
rules.unknown_field: the object has a member that its schema does not have
rules.missing_field: the object lacks a member that its schema requires
rules.out_of_range: an integer is outside its range, or a list or a map has too few or too many entries
rules.bad_text: a string is not one of the values allowed, or has a wrong length or a character outside its alphabet
rules.bad_address: a string is not an address of this network
rules.bad_key: a string is not the text form of a public key of scheme 1
rules.bad_signature: a string is not the text form of a signature of scheme 1
rules.inconsistent: a rule that ties several fields together is broken

directives.$ref: the object of the accepted vector of that name, which stands earlier in the file
directives.$index: inside the item of a $list or of a $map, the number of the item, from 0, plus the argument; elsewhere, the argument
directives.$key: the text form of the 1,984 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, key N'), N being the argument in decimal
directives.$sig: the text form of the 3,373 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, signature N')
directives.$address: the address of this network whose hash is the 48 bytes SHAKE256('kern schema vectors, address N')
directives.$text: [count, piece]: the piece written count times
directives.$concat: [parts]: the parts one after the other, an integer in decimal
directives.$list: [count, item]: a list of count items
directives.$map: [count, name, value]: an object of count members
